harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Recovered both staged print jobs into a persistent CUPS queue named archive. Their raw bytes are archived under /srv/legacy2/print-spool-recovery/printed, the original spool files remain intact, and the configuration survived node1’s reboot.
actions_performed: Installed CentOS 5-compatible CUPS 1.3.7 packages without changing the OS release or kernel.
Created an atomic, retry-idempotent archive backend and SELinux-compatible printed directory.
Created and enabled the raw CUPS queue archive.
Submitted J100 and J101 exactly once; both completed successfully.
Verified exactly two archived files, each byte-identical to its original spool payload.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified CUPS, queue state, job history, and archived data recovered.

evidence.requirement: Working CUPS archive queue for raw jobs
evidence.summary: Shows the running CUPS service, archive backend and queue, two raw submissions, successful completion, and resulting archive files.

evidence.requirement: Process every manifest job exactly once
evidence.summary: Shows exactly two manifest jobs, exactly two submissions/completions, no pending jobs, and exactly two output files.

evidence.requirement: Retain payload bytes and original spool files
evidence.summary: Original and archived sizes and byte comparisons match for J100 and J101; jobs.tsv and both original .prn files remain present.

evidence.requirement: Keep installed OS release and kernel

evidence.summary: Captures healthy baseline boot ID d9967662-2c50-4957-8000-000000000000, acknowledged safe reboot, new boot ID 72b53ef1-c7a6-4d45-8000-000000000000, and recovered service, queue, two completed jobs, two archived files, matching hashes, and retained originals.
